newsitem.title: USA: Trimble to cut 10 percent of workforce.
newsitem.headline: Trimble to cut 10 percent of workforce.

text.p: Trimble said it will cut 10 percent of its workforce and and consolidate certain manufacturing facilities and service organizations as part of a corporate restructuring program.

The company said it expects to report a loss in the third quarter ending September 30, which will include a charge from the restructuring. It also expects to report third quarter revenues "at or below" second quarter levels.
As part of the restructuring, it is consolidating into three business units: Commercial Systems, Software and Component Technologies and Aerospace.
The company said the 10 percent workforce cut will amount to roughly 100 employees being laid off.
It said it had second quarter revenues of $58.6 million. In last year's third quarter it earned $4.3 million or $0.20 per share, on revenues of $62.8 million.
Trimble sad that while it is experiencing growth in unit volume with lower-priced, high margin new products, "we are not experiencing the historical seasonal increase in total revenues."

"It is necesary to consolidate our operations to bring expenses more in line with revenues and we will continue to evaluate these cost reduction measures based on market demand," Charles Trimble, chairman and chief executive officer said.
